programmes.d: This episode is a real balancing act when expert balancer Ed Kennedy graces the stage along with comic legend Buddy Hackett and Breakfast Club star Ally Sheedy.
TV comedy icon Bob Newhart stops by, along with Saundra Santiago and Teresa Ganzel.
The laughs can't stop/won't stop when comedy heavyweights Jack Lemmon and Steven Wright stop by the set.
What do you get when you combine comedian Don Rickles, 95-year-old artist Jon Serl and a Johnny Carson monologue that mentions Pee-wee Herman and Russian Big Macs? Watch this episode to find out!
Nine-time Emmy winner Carl Reiner loves talking about the World Series and his days in the Army! Comedian David Brenner covers LA earthquakes.
Carl Reiner insists that Johnny is a great role model for dating couples. Reflects on shaving his head for a movie, and trades quips on aging with French beauty Catherine Deneuve.
Carl Reiner improvises an Italian aria and riffs on ridiculous celebrity stories from the tabloids. Olympic diver Greg Louganis shows off his moves on a trampoline.
Comedy master Carl Reiner ate his way through France and now complains to Johnny about his weight gain. Shows a clip from his movie, Summer Rentals.
TV's ultimate GOAT Carl Reiner performs a dance number then chats about writing screenplays and (wait for it) the Supreme Court.
TV's polymath Carl Reiner chats about his wife Estelle, a recent nose injury, his frequent forgetfulness, and the smash hit flick When Harry Met Sally written and directed by his son, Rob Reiner.
Comic genius Carl Reiner makes his 46th visit to Johnny's couch. Discusses his attempts at dieting and presents Johnny with a bunch of gifts: slippers, pipe, glasses and....a gun.

Wild and crazy guy Steve Martin does card tricks, George Foreman talks winning the heavyweight championship and Johnny details his valentine from Don Rickles. Sandy Duncan and Binnie Barnes also appear.
Johnny gives questionable amounts of respect to Rodney Dangerfield, then reasonable amounts of respect to Dom Deluise, Orson Bean and Mariette Hartley.

George Carlin sticks only to words you CAN say on TV. Plus, Rita Reutter is an older sex symbol, McLean Stevenson had a date with the Rose Bowl Queen and Martina Navratilova is the best tennis player in the world.
Carol Burnett reveals her Hollywood idols, Tim Conway details losing his car at a party and Johnny discusses The Joy Of Sex. Plus, Robert Easton and Tracee Talavera appear.
George Carlin likes to harmonize on the phone with the dial tone. In case you needed more reasons to watch this episode, Keshia Knight Pulliam also appears.
Michael Palin sleeps all night and works all day, but still finds time to stop by the couch. Mariette Hartley talks practical jokes and Johnny takes on Leave It To Beaver.
A stand-up routine by comic giant George Carlin highlights this episode which also features record-setting test pilot Chuck Yeager.
The queen of comedy, Carol Burnett dishes on Hollywood High, reminisces about her family, and her early days on The Garry Moore Show. Bob Hope chats about politics.
Comedy genius and Carol Burnett co-star Tim Conway discusses his movie, "Long Shot," marriage, and horseracing. Hal Linden joins in.
Tim Conway and Harry Anderson stop by to chat with Johnny.
TV'S Funniest guy, Tim Conway chats about his 7, count 'em 7, kids and his career as a practical joker, while in the service.
Comedian Steve Martin creates mayhem punching Santa backstage then sitting on his lap on Johnny's couch. Steve is ticked off that his cats didn't recognize him after he'd been away for 8 months.
Stand up legend Paul Lynde spills the beans on his family life, career and love of Houston, TX. Special attention to his fans and his many stints on Hollywood Squares.
Charles Grodin is Johnny's guest, and 'Welcome Back Kotter' star Gabe Kaplan pokes fun at his hometown Brooklyn and his high school days, upon which Kotter was based.
